lesson.subject: general-knowledge
lesson.title: Different and Equal
lesson.summary: Learn why stereotypes and unfair treatment harm people and how to treat everyone fairly.
learning_objectives: Know how to challenge them safely

standards.text: Respect for others, challenging stereotypes, and rules and laws that protect people

success_criteria: I can explain what a stereotype is
I can say why stereotypes are unfair
I can say what to do and who to tell
lesson.real_life: Pakistani-British communities and UK law (the Equality Act 2010), the Constitution of Pakistan on equal citizens, and the Prophet's last sermon on equality.

options.text: Speak up kindly or tell a trusted adult

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how can we treat everyone fairly?
blocks.say: Today we think about fairness. Everyone is different, and everyone deserves respect.

blocks.caption: Children celebrating after a game of cricket at sunset.
blocks.credit: Photo by vicky adams on Unsplash
blocks.say: Children play cricket in many places, and anyone can join the game.

blocks.text: Stop 1: A belief with no evidence

blocks.markdown: An **assumption** is a belief we have without checking the facts.
blocks.say: An assumption is something we believe without checking. It might be wrong.

blocks.markdown: A **stereotype** is a fixed idea about a whole group of people.
blocks.say: A stereotype is a fixed idea about a whole group. It ignores that people differ.

scenes.caption: Checked.

options.text: A belief we have without checking the facts

blocks.markdown: **Prejudice** is an unfair opinion formed before knowing someone.
blocks.say: Stereotypes spread through jokes, pictures and things people repeat. They can seem normal.

blocks.alt: Eight hands in colourful knitted sleeves reaching into the centre of a circle and piling on top of each other
blocks.caption: Hands piled together in a circle. A fair team makes room for everyone.
blocks.credit: Photo by Hannah Busing on Unsplash
blocks.say: Stereotypes can make people feel they cannot join in, try or belong.

scenes.caption: Repeating.
scenes.say: Someone repeats an idea about a group.

scenes.caption: Spreading.
scenes.say: Others hear it and start to believe it.

scenes.caption: Left out.
scenes.say: People are limited or left out.

question.prompt: Stereotypes can stop people from joining in.
question.explanation: Stereotypes can limit what people try.

blocks.title: Hina and the winning run
blocks.transcript: Hina watches her classmates choose teams for cricket. Someone says a girl cannot play cricket. Hina asks kindly, how do you know that? They have no evidence. It is only an assumption. The captain gives the girl a turn to bat. She hits the ball and scores the winning run. Everyone cheers. The stereotype was wrong. Hina smiles. Everyone deserves a fair chance.
blocks.caption: Hina notices her classmates assume a girl cannot play cricket, and they show how she scores the winning run.

points: A stereotype is a fixed idea about a group
blocks.say: Let us remember. Assumptions and stereotypes can be unfair, and we can check them.

blocks.text: Stop 1: The Equality Act in simple words

blocks.markdown: It covers things like age, race, religion, disability and sex.
blocks.say: In the UK, a law called the Equality Act 2010 protects people from unfair treatment.

blocks.alt: White cricket stumps with orange bails in the foreground and a large stadium behind on a green field
blocks.caption: Cricket stumps on a pitch. Fair play means the same rules for everyone.
blocks.credit: Photo by Sudhakar Chandra on Unsplash
blocks.say: Pakistan's Constitution also says that all citizens are equal before the law.

blocks.markdown: **Ageism** is unfair treatment because of someone's age.
blocks.say: Ageism is treating people unfairly because of their age. It can affect children and older people.

blocks.markdown: An **upstander** speaks up or helps when someone is treated unfairly.
blocks.say: An upstander helps when something is unfair. You can speak kindly and calmly.

scenes.caption: Calm words.
scenes.say: Say: I do not agree, and here is why.

scenes.caption: Include.
scenes.say: Say: let us ask her if she wants to play.

scenes.caption: Support.
scenes.say: Stand next to your friend to show support.

blocks.markdown: Telling an adult helps keep people safe.
blocks.say: If someone is hurt or still unfair, tell a trusted adult. This is not tale-telling.

scenes.caption: Teacher.
scenes.say: A teacher at school can help.

scenes.caption: Family.
scenes.say: A parent or carer at home can help.

scenes.caption: Community.
scenes.say: Imams, teachers and elders in our community can also give advice.

blocks.markdown: No person is better than another except by good character and kindness.
blocks.say: Islam teaches that people are equal. In his last sermon, the Prophet reminded everyone of this.
